title: Stakeholder Conversation: Prepare Your Questions
description: Use AI follow-up questions to sharpen the validation questions you will ask a real stakeholder.

questions.prompt: Share the three validation questions you plan to ask, the stakeholder role you hope to ask, and what you need to learn from the conversation. Then name the single riskiest assumption in your current frame, the stakeholder who can help test it, and the evidence, not approval, that would change your mind.
questions.placeholder: Include the stakeholder role, your three draft questions, and the assumption or uncertainty each question is meant to test. Add your riskiest assumption, who can test it, and what evidence would confirm or complicate it.
questions.aiContext: This is Sprint 3 of Reframing Problems with AI. The participant is preparing questions for a real stakeholder conversation. Push for listening rather than pitching, evidence rather than approval, and questions that uncover needs, constraints, tensions, and assumptions. Diagnose each question as leading, vague, or missing evidence. Challenge yes-or-no questions, leading questions, and questions that ask stakeholders to solve the participant's assignment. Also push the participant to distinguish real listening and evidence from approval-seeking, to mark each need as confirmed or inferred, and to resist replacing a real stakeholder conversation with AI prediction.
questions.discussionPrompt: Use these questions to refine your validation plan. Your final response should include three stronger stakeholder questions and explain what each one is meant to test.
questions.summaryPlaceholder: Rewrite your three validation questions. Include the stakeholder role, what each question tests, and what would count as useful evidence. Name your riskiest assumption, who can test it, and what evidence would confirm or complicate your frame.
